Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment findings (transcript): Progressive (~2 weeks) left-sided arm numbness/tingling and subjective weakness involving elbow, arm, and palmar surface of digits 2–4; intermittent shoulder pain with movement; functional impairment (difficulty with piano, occasional dropping). Recent transient left-eye visual field loss (~20 minutes) a few weeks ago. Recent viral/flu-like illness ~1 month prior. No objective exam findings documented in transcript.
- Integrating DDx (consistent items): DDx supports several plausible causes consistent with history:
  - Cervical radiculopathy (high likelihood per DDx) — fits progressive unilateral arm sensory symptoms after new repetitive upper-limb activity (boxing) and proximal symptoms.
  - Peripheral median neuropathy / carpal tunnel (medium likelihood) — palmar numbness in digits 2–4 maps to median nerve distribution but proximal symptoms less typical.
  - Multiple sclerosis (medium likelihood per DDx and clinician concern) — transient visual disturbance and later separated sensory symptoms are features that warrant consideration and neurologic imaging.
- Clinical plan from transcript: Urgent neurology referral and brain imaging recommended. No acute medications started. Steroids discussed as a possible treatment for an acute inflammatory demyelinating episode but were not prescribed pending diagnostic workup. Safety-net: go to Emergency Department if weakness progresses (especially to legs), or if severe headache, vomiting, seizures/fits, or worsening visual symptoms occur.
- Conflicts/uncertainties: Clinician emphasized need to exclude demyelinating central causes (e.g., MS). DDx ranks cervical radiculopathy as the most likely diagnosis. Both possibilities are plausible given the history; this represents a difference in emphasis between clinician impression and the DDx ranking — conflict noted. No objective neurologic examination or imaging is available to confirm any diagnosis.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Cervical radiculopathy (cervical disc herniation / foraminal compression) — Likelihood: High.
  - Justification: Progressive unilateral arm/elbow/palmar sensory symptoms and subjective motor involvement after initiation of vigorous upper-limb activity (boxing); proximal involvement and shoulder movement–provoked discomfort support a proximal mechanical nerve-root process.
- Median neuropathy / peripheral median nerve compression (carpal tunnel) — Likelihood: Moderate.
  - Justification: Palmar numbness of digits 2–4 maps to median nerve distribution and accounts for fine-motor functional impairment; rapid proximal progression and elbow/arm symptoms make isolated carpal tunnel less likely.
- Multiple sclerosis (inflammatory demyelinating disease) — Likelihood: Moderate.
  - Justification: Transient unilateral visual disturbance and subsequent separated-in-time focal sensory/motor symptoms are compatible with demyelinating disease; clinician expressed concern and recommended neurology/imaging.
